content.value: The factorial n! of a positive integer is defined by ${ \mathfrak { n } } ! = { \mathfrak { n } } . ( { \mathfrak { n } } - 1 ) . ( { \mathfrak { n } } - 2 ) . . . . 1$ , where O! =1. Write a user- defined function that calculates the factorial n! of a number. For function name and arguments use y = fact (x), where the input argument xis the number whose factorial is to be calculated and the output arguments y is the value x! . The function displays an error-message if a negative or non-integer number is entered when the function is ca1Jed. Do not use Octave's built-in function 'factorial'
